title: No Heroes Allowed!
subtitle: Build the dungeon the hero is trying to conquer
summary: No Heroes Allowed! is Japan Studio and Acquire's PSP strategy game, first released in Japan on 11 March 2010. The player digs a dungeon and encourages monsters to develop within it, defending the demon lord from approaching adventurers. The usual role-playing objective is reversed: the heroic intruder is the problem to be solved. The maze has to support the creatures that protect it as well as delay the visitors. A successful defence therefore begins long before the hero arrives, through the shape of the tunnels and the life the player allows to grow inside them.
body: No Heroes Allowed! is Japan Studio and Acquire's PSP strategy game, first released in Japan on 11 March 2010. The player digs a dungeon and encourages monsters to develop within it, defending the demon lord from approaching adventurers. The usual role-playing objective is reversed: the heroic intruder is the problem to be solved. The maze has to support the creatures that protect it as well as delay the visitors. A successful defence therefore begins long before the hero arrives, through the shape of the tunnels and the life the player allows to grow inside them.

Digging changes the underground environment, creating routes and opportunities for different creatures. The player manages that system indirectly, relying on the inhabitants to confront the heroes rather than controlling each fighter individually. Water and aquatic monsters expand the possibilities in this third entry, adding another condition to the dungeon's design. A new passage can help the defence or give an invader a more convenient route, so every opening needs a purpose. The challenge lies in arranging an environment whose inhabitants can do useful work once the player is no longer deciding every movement.

The Japanese title presents it as the third What Did I Do to Deserve This, My Lord? game, while the Western name makes its reversed premise immediately clear. Badman's daughter Badnella joins the cast and supports a multiplayer mode built around the pair. North America received a digital edition in November 2010. Later PlayStation reissues kept the original PSP game available. Its humour and strategy share the same foundation: the familiar dungeon is understood from the other side, where an efficient hero is a destructive intruder and a healthy monster population is something worth protecting.
story_headings: Build the dungeon the hero is trying to conquer
A monster needs an ecosystem, not only a room
A clearer name for a mischievous series
